title: Everything in Sonar
sub: Every capability, from device discovery to packet-level evidence, without sending a single packet to your machines.

items: Devices found from traffic alone, with no active scanning
IP, MAC address, vendor and running services for each device
Each device mapped to its site, role and segment
See who talks to whom across the site
Unlisted devices and services shown in their own table
Import your existing list, or add devices manually or by CSV
Commands recorded down to function and target address

Manufacturing and process: Modbus, S7comm, EtherNet/IP (CIP), PROFINET, OPC UA
Also EtherCAT, Omron FINS, GE SRTP and HART-IP

Connections to sensitive countries and random-looking domain names
Large transfers and unusually long connections
Threat intelligence matches, such as Tor exit nodes

Every incident scored for severity from 0 to 100
Scoring and sensitive-country list tuned to your site

specs.v: Passive site sensors, on-premises hub, air-gapped option
Sensor from 4 cores, 8 GB RAM; hub from 8 cores, 24 GB RAM
SIEM and SOC tools, AutoSecOps, MISP, STIX/TAXII, REST API
Incident reporting under Türkiye’s Law No. 7545, audits and insurers
Local accounts, LDAP or SSO; encrypted console and sensor traffic
Packets and files stay on the sensor; nothing flows outward

top: Every device and command on record
gaps: Scope limits buyers will ask about: serial protocols and encrypted traffic are not decoded, and Sonar never scans actively. The deck states this openly.
Jaguar Land Rover, 2025: five weeks of shutdown because it could not see whether attackers reached its plants. The deck’s lead story; the page omits it.
Law No. 7545: withholding information carries 1–3 years in prison; critical sectors named May 2026: energy, finance, healthcare, transportation, water.
